change: No change. Primary forearms->Wrist Extensors is correct. Secondary empty is correct — this is a strict isolation exercise with no meaningful secondary muscle engagement.

Removed 'Abductor->Abductor' from primary. The original listed Abductor (tensor fasciae latae / hip abductor bucket) as a primary mover, but the hip drive in the kipping pull-up is produced by hip flexors (iliopsoas) which have no valid mapping in the allowed bucket/latin list — they cannot be represented and are omitted per rules. Glutes (Gluteus Maximus) added as secondary: EMG and biomechanics sources confirm hip extension by the glutes is a key driver of the kipping swing's upward momentum. NOTE: Hip flexors are genuinely engaged as a primary mover in the kip but have no allowed mapping — flagged for user.

Removed 'Abductor->Abductor' from primary. The original used Abductor to represent hip flexors (iliopsoas), which is incorrect — Abductor maps to hip abductors/tensor fasciae, not hip flexors. Hip flexors are the true primary driver of leg elevation in the L-sit but have no valid bucket/latin mapping and are omitted per rules. Moved Triceps from secondary to primary: research consistently identifies triceps as a primary mover (they lock the elbow and provide the pressing force to elevate the body). Removed 'forearms->Wrist Extensors' from secondary: in a pressing/gripping context only Wrist Flexors stabilize the wrist; extensors are not meaningfully loaded. Added 'mid back->Lower Traps' to secondary: scapular depression (lower trapezius) is well-documented as a significant stabilizer in the L-sit. NOTE: Hip flexors (iliopsoas) are a true primary mover but unmappable — flagged for user.
No change. Primary (Quads, Glutes, Obliques) and secondary (Hamstrings, Abs, Anterior Deltoids, Lower Back) are accurate for this combined lunge-with-rotation exercise.

Added 'Sternal Head' to chest primary. The landmine press arcs upward at roughly 30-45 degrees — research shows this angle activates clavicular head preferentially but the sternal head also contributes meaningfully (unlike a strict incline where sternal head drops off). Both heads are engaged in this movement. Added 'Lower Back->Erector Spinae' to secondary: the alternating lunge component in a standing free-weight movement loads the erector spinae as a spinal stabilizer throughout.
